sources.entry: Visual Studio Code - Code editor developed by Microsoft.

summary.one_liner: Microsoft's open-source source repository ("Code - OSS") for the Visual Studio Code code editor, which is also the base for the official VS Code distribution.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes this repository as where Microsoft develops Visual Studio Code together with the community, including code, issues, roadmap, monthly iteration plans, and endgame plans. Visual Studio Code is a distribution of this code with Microsoft-specific customizations under a Microsoft product license. The editor combines code editing, navigation, and understanding support with lightweight debugging, an extensibility model, and integration with existing tools. Built-in extensions for grammars, snippets, and language features are located in an extensions folder. The README also documents a development container for Dev Containers and GitHub Codespaces, and points to a wiki for building from source, testing, and contributing guidelines.
use_cases: Read or modify the source code of the VS Code editor
Contribute bug fixes or features to an open-source code editor
Report bugs or request features for VS Code
Set up a containerized development environment for editor development
Study how an extensible code editor is structured
how_to_run: Clone the repository (see How to Contribute document for build and run from source instructions)
Optionally open in a Dev Containers volume using the 'Dev Containers: Clone Repository in Container Volume...' command
Optionally use the 'Codespaces: Create New Codespace' command with the GitHub Codespaces extension
notable: Official source repository for Visual Studio Code, developed by Microsoft with the community
Publishes roadmap, monthly iteration plans, and endgame plans openly
Includes a Dev Containers / GitHub Codespaces development container
Bundled extensions provide grammars, snippets, and language features for many languages
caveats: A full build requires at least 4 cores and 6 GB RAM (8 GB recommended) in the Docker or Codespace environment
Official Visual Studio Code binaries are released under a Microsoft product license rather than MIT; only the Code - OSS source is MIT
